notable_absence.finding: There is no add-function or remove-function endpoint, and no partial-update semantics anywhere in this API: POST /evaluator/v1/libraries/{library} always replaces the ENTIRE library body, and the page's own NOTE spells out the workaround three times over - 'To add a function to a library, update the library with all existing functions, plus the new function', 'To update a function, update the library with all existing functions, including the updated function definition', 'To delete a function from a library, update the library with all existing functions, without the deleted function.' Every one of the four curl examples (Add/Edit/Delete under Create or Update a Library) demonstrates this same read-modify-resend-the-whole-library pattern rather than a per-function operation. This is a real, load-bearing REST design fact - a client cannot safely add one function without first reading the current library contents - and it is not captured by any relation in this record because no predicate in the registry expresses 'lacks a finer-grained operation'; doesNotSupport is the closest promoted fit but its examples are all feature/edition boundaries, not API granularity, so I have left it as a finding rather than force the mapping.

cross_component_finding:
js-udf:library (minted in round 10's server/8.0/n1ql/n1ql-rest-api/intro.json, unpromoted) and js-udf:udf-library (promoted, first minted in cloud/guides/create-javascript-library.json) both describe the exact same object - a named container of one or more JavaScript functions addressable at global or bucket.scope granularity - and neither record's author appears to have checked the other before minting. js-udf:library's own label ('JavaScript library for SQL++ user-defined functions') and js-udf:udf-library's label ('UDF library (container for 1 or more JavaScript functions, shareable across user-defined functions)') are different words for one thing, and this page confirms it structurally: its 'Library' definition (name/bucket/scope/code) is exactly what js-udf:udf-library's promoted description says it is. This record uses js-udf:udf-library throughout and does not reuse js-udf:library, so as not to keep propagating the fork forward; reconciliation should retire js-udf:library into js-udf:udf-library the same way earlier rounds folded requiresMinVersionFor into availableSince.

Separately, worth flagging for the admin-page's already-recorded finding that the Admin API 'mirrors the system keyspaces': this page shows the SAME shape one level up - GET /evaluator/v1/libraries (Read All Libraries) and the SQL++-side introspection of UDF libraries (documented elsewhere in the n1ql: language-reference pages, not read in this batch) are almost certainly two access surfaces onto one underlying store, following the identical pattern already flagged for /admin/*. Not asserted as a relation here for the same reason: no sentence on this page states the identity outright.
cross_product_finding: No Capella counterpart directory exists for n1ql-rest-functions (cloud/n1ql/ has no equivalent REST page), consistent with round 10's finding that the whole n1ql-rest-api-style REST surface is Server-only. Capella's own JavaScript-UDF-library guides (cloud/guides/create-javascript-library.json, which is where js-udf:udf-library was first promoted) document library creation exclusively through the Capella UI / Query Workbench, never through a directly-addressed REST endpoint on a Query Service port - the same data-plane-shared-but-differently-reached split already recorded for the query-execution and admin REST surfaces. This page's global-vs-scoped library distinction and its two dedicated RBAC roles (Manage Global External Functions / Manage Scope External Functions) also have no stated Capella equivalent: Capella's UDF guides describe permissions in terms of Capella's own cluster-access-credential model, not these two Server RBAC roles.
